page: Amazon Web Services r5a.large is an entry-tier instance in the AMD-powered memory-optimized R5a family, managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provisions two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an AMD EPYC 7571 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Its memory subsystem provides 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes local instance storage, requiring network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the entry-level compute density and older Zen-generation architecture of the AMD EPYC 7571. In compute assessments, the instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 1825.52, a single-core Geekbench score of 712.0, and a multi-core Geekbench score of 948.0, positioning it in the lowest decile of modern cloud benchmarks. Cryptographic throughput reached 1601.68 on PassMark CPU encryption tests, aided by hardware AES and SHA extensions. Memory bandwidth peaked at 77.09 GB/sec for small cached reads, falling to 21.22 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 12.29 GB/sec for large block writes. In application benchmarks, Redis processed 1.24 million SET operations per second, while static web throughput reached 1.59 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency for the r5a.large is centered on memory density rather than raw compute speed. While single-thread and parallel CPU performance are constrained by the two-thread limit and older core architecture, the instance provides access to a 16 GB memory pool at an entry resource profile. Primary tradeoffs include the absence of integrated NVMe storage and basic 1 Gbps networking. This instance matches memory-heavy, low-compute workloads, including small in-memory caches, development database instances, lightweight background data processing, and auxiliary microservices requiring substantial RAM headroom.
description: Amazon Web Services r5a.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features two dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz, supported by 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz. The hardware profile delivers an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation but does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark measurements reflect modest compute capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 948.0, a PassMark CPU score of 1825.52, and Redis throughput of 1.24 million SET operations per second. The server offers cost efficiency for memory-sensitive configurations that do not demand extensive computational capacity, serving as an appropriate fit for small-scale caching layers, low-traffic relational databases, and lightweight backend services requiring dedicated memory capacity.
